$comment: Fuel catalog v0.1 (spec §8.5). Values taken VERBATIM from docs/research-notes.md §4 with their source_id, basis and original unit. Primary source: UK DESNZ 2025 (uk-desnz-ghg-2025) — density + NCV/GCV both bases + CO2/CH4/N2O split. Global/rank fallback: IPCC 2006 (ipcc-2006-v2) for crude oil, anthracite, lignite. NOTE ON UNITS: DESNZ publishes gravimetric energy as GJ/tonne, which is numerically identical to MJ/kg (1 GJ/tonne = 1 MJ/kg) — stored as mj_per_kg with the GJ/tonne origin noted, no silent conversion. Per-litre / per-m³ figures are DESNZ's own kWh/L, kWh/m³ (Net/Gross CV) columns. IPCC NCVs in TJ/Gg = GJ/tonne = MJ/kg. Missing properties are OMITTED (UI shows 'not available') — never invented (rulebook, AGENTS.md). Every heating_value carries basis + >=1 source_refs; density carries >=1 source_refs. See src/lib/data/schemas.ts (fuelSchema).

heating_values.notes: IPCC 2006 Vol.2 Ch.1 Table 1.2 'Crude Oil' NCV = 42.3 TJ/Gg = 42.3 GJ/tonne = 42.3 MJ/kg (global default, net/LHV basis). 95% CI 40.1–44.8. DESNZ 2025 has no generic 'crude oil' row (it covers refined products), so IPCC is primary here per research-notes §6.

fuels.typical_ranges: Physical crude density varies by grade (~800–950 kg/m³, light vs heavy); a serious primary density was NOT FOUND in this pass, so density is omitted. Energy per physical barrel is an estimate (~5.6–6.3 GJ) and is NOT the same as 'boe' (fixed 5.8 MMBTU convention).
fuels.notes: Generic crude oil, modeled on IPCC 2006 global defaults (rulebook C.3). No DESNZ entry. Density deliberately omitted (not available in a serious primary source in the v0.1 research pass) so volume↔mass shows 'not available' rather than an invented number.
warnings: Crude oil is not a single substance: density and energy content vary by grade (API gravity). Any barrel↔energy or volume↔mass figure for crude is an ESTIMATE, not a measured property of a specific oil.
A physical barrel of crude is NOT the same as 'boe' (barrel of oil equivalent), which is a fixed 5.8 MMBTU energy-equivalence convention.

Volumetric Net CV derived from DESNZ density 0.802 kg/m³ × 12.707 kWh/kg = 10.191 kWh/m³. DERIVED (not a verbatim DESNZ cell) — DESNZ's own per-litre-of-gas figure (0.01 kWh/L) rounds too coarsely to use directly. Range reflects typical pipeline-gas variability. Reference T/P unstated (see warning).

Volumetric Gross CV derived from DESNZ density 0.802 kg/m³ × 14.077 kWh/kg = 11.290 kWh/m³. DERIVED from DESNZ density × gravimetric GCV (both verbatim), not a verbatim cell. ~11 kWh/m³ is the typical UK gas-bill figure. Reference T/P unstated (see warning).

fuels.notes: DESNZ 2025 'Natural gas' (UK grid mix). The per-m³ heating values are DERIVED from DESNZ's verbatim density and gravimetric CV (marked in each entry's notes), because DESNZ's volumetric cell is rounded to 0.01 kWh/L. IPCC 2006 Natural Gas NCV 48.0 MJ/kg, CO2 56,100 kg/TJ. EIA US: 1,036 Btu/scf, 54.81 kg CO2/Mcf. LNG, CNG and pure methane are separate entries.
warnings: Natural gas m³→energy is NOT an exact identity. The reference temperature and pressure (normal m³ at 0 °C vs standard m³ at 15/25 °C) are NOT stated by the source, and real energy content varies by field, network and time.

This is NOT how a gas bill is calculated: billing uses your supplier's local calorific value (Brennwert) and a state-correction number (Zustandszahl) that maps your meter's operating-condition m³ to reference energy. Do not use this result for billing disputes.

DESNZ lists NO combustion CO2/CO2e factor for pure methane as a distinct row (it is a properties reference). No emission factor is attached here rather than reusing natural gas's (which is a grid mix, not pure CH4) — a combustion CO2 for methane is therefore 'not available' in v0.1 sources. IPCC has no separate methane row either; natural gas is the closest analog.

fuels.notes: DESNZ 2025 'LNG' — chemically natural gas, but ~600× denser in energy per volume than gaseous natural gas. Per-litre CO2e in DESNZ = 1.17797 kgCO2e/L. The per-L heating value is derived from DESNZ's liquid density × gravimetric CV.
warnings: 1 m³ (or 1 L) of LIQUEFIED natural gas is NOT the same as 1 m³ of GASEOUS natural gas: LNG is ~600× denser in energy per volume. Never convert LNG volume directly to gas volume — go via mass/energy. This entry is the liquid phase.

density.notes: Gas density 0.08988 kg/m³ at STP (0 °C, 1 atm). Liquid hydrogen at its boiling point (−252.87 °C) is ~70.8 kg/m³ (not stored as the primary density — H2 is normally handled by mass). Source h2tools (cross-source-verified; see sources.json).

heating_values.notes: LHV 119.96 MJ/kg (≈ 33.3 kWh/kg). h2tools / DOE-derived, cross-source-verified (primary page returned HTTP 403 on automated fetch; re-checked by follow-up).

HHV 141.79 MJ/kg (≈ 39.4 kWh/kg), NIST Chemistry WebBook (SRD 69)-traceable printed value (285.83 kJ/mol). The DOE GREET/ORNL table gives 142.18 MJ/kg (gaseous) — hence the range. Earlier project figure 141.88 was between these; corrected to the NIST-printed 141.79. The LHV/HHV gap is large for hydrogen (~18%) because all combustion product is water.

fuels.notes: Hydrogen physical properties. Direct combustion CO2 = 0 (no carbon in the molecule) — handled by the engine as an exact physical fact, NOT via an emission factor. NOT FOUND in DESNZ 2025 or IPCC 2006 (both are fossil/biomass-scoped). No upstream/production emission factor is included in v0.1 (grey/blue/green H2 differ enormously) — upstream is out of scope and must NOT be implied as zero.
warnings: Direct combustion of hydrogen emits no CO2 (no carbon), but this is a COMBUSTION-ONLY figure. Upstream production emissions are NOT zero and depend entirely on the pathway (grey/SMR vs blue vs green) — they are not included here.
Hydrogen's LHV and HHV differ by ~18% — always check which basis a hydrogen energy figure uses.

heating_values.notes: IPCC 2006 Vol.2 Ch.1 Table 1.2 'Lignite' NCV = 11.9 TJ/Gg = 11.9 GJ/tonne = 11.9 MJ/kg (global default, net basis). 95% CI 5.50–21.6 — very wide, reflecting lignite's highly variable moisture/ash content. fuels.notes: Lignite (brown coal), IPCC 2006 global default (rulebook §4.9, research-notes §6). DESNZ uses functional not rank-based coal categories, so IPCC's rank-based Table 1.2/2.2 is used. No density in the source → volume conversions not available. HHV/GCV not available from IPCC (Table 1.2 gives NCV only) → shows 'not available'.
warnings: Lignite is extremely variable (moisture/ash): the IPCC net calorific value has a 95% range of 5.5–21.6 MJ/kg. Treat any lignite energy figure as a rough estimate. No density available → volume conversions not available.

heating_values.notes: IPCC 2006 Vol.2 Ch.1 Table 1.2 'Anthracite' NCV = 26.7 TJ/Gg = 26.7 GJ/tonne = 26.7 MJ/kg (global default, net basis). 95% CI 21.6–32.2. DESNZ 2025 has no 'anthracite' row, so IPCC is primary (research-notes §6).
